equivalence_analysis: Our explicit N=3 real-Fourier coordinate calculation turns a fixed signed DC component and a fixed conjugate-pair modulus into a circle; the binary alphabet becomes a rotated cube. This places the constraint geometry in an established class. Generic rotations and other finite alphabets need not equal that exact Fourier instance. Different input sets do not prove inequivalent attractor dynamics.
